description.en: Under the Franco-British convention of 23 Dec 1920 the northern frontier ran along the middle of the Jordan and Lake Tiberias, with a Golan triangle (apex at Quneitra) inside Palestine; the eastern shore strip of the lake was outside it.

sources.quote: The frontier was to run in the middle of the Jordan River and of Lake Tiberias, with one exception: a triangular area on the Golan, with Quneitra at the head of the triangle, was included within Palestine.
Franco-British convention on certain points connected with the mandates for Syria and the Lebanon, Palestine and Mesopotamia

notes.en: Only one opened source (Blum) gives the Golan-triangle detail; ECF confirms the 1923 agreement amended the 1920 one. Mark the Golan part as schematic. The eastern boundary was laid down by a British memorandum of 16 Sept 1922 (ICJ 2004, para. 70).

description.en: Mandate Palestine within its final boundaries: 1923 Paulet-Newcombe line in the north (Golan to the French Mandate; Lake Tiberias and the Jordan wholly in Palestine), the eastern boundary with Transjordan per the 1922 memorandum and 1928 treaty, and the pre-war line with Egypt in the south-west.

sources.quote: It amended the previous agreement from 1920, and left the entirety of the Golan Heights under French control, while the Sea of Galilee was given to Palestine.
Exchange of notes constituting an agreement between the British and French governments respecting the boundary line between Syria and Palestine from the Mediterranean to El Hamme
on the eastern border by a British memorandum of 16 September 1922 and an Anglo-Transjordanian Treaty of 20 February 1928.

notes.en: The 1923 agreement took the form of an exchange of notes dated 7 March 1923 (UN treaty list; ECF). Blum states the Golan triangle was transferred 'in 1923, to accommodate an influential sheikh' - a motive given by one author only.
